about.title: The Studio
about.statement: Infanti is a stop motion animation studio founded by two Belgian sisters, Louise and Margot. After following different yet complementary career paths, they launched a project in late January 2024 that they had been dreaming about for a long time: working together to create stop motion animation videos.
about.approach: Working within tight budget and time constraints, they strive to build poetic and surprising worlds — small universes that, in just a few seconds, can evoke emotion and invite the viewer's imagination to expand the story or world beyond what is shown. Their work is crafted almost exclusively using needle-felted wool, chosen both for its aesthetic qualities and for the transparency and flexibility it allows.
about.philosophy: They intentionally preserve a raw and imperfect aesthetic in their videos, allowing the texture and magic of stop motion to come through the screen. Their approach stands in contrast to the rise of AI-generated imagery and its often polished, seamless look. Instead, they aim to highlight the value of handcraft and the beauty of imperfection.

louise.name: Louise Infanti
louise.bio: Louise is an illustrator, comic book artist, and stop motion animator. She graduated from the École de Recherche Graphique in Brussels and later completed several training programs at Technocité in Mons, focusing on animation, rigging, and storyboarding. She is in charge of storyboarding, animation, and post-production.

margot.name: Margot Infanti
margot.bio: Margot is a director and stop motion animator. Trained as an actress at the Conservatoire of Brussels, she worked between theatrical roles and teaching. She led puppet-making workshops in Hablingbo, Sweden — an experience that highlighted her long-standing love for crafting. She focuses mainly on directing, crafting, and animation.

methodology.title: Our Methodology
methodology.metaTitle: Methodology — From Screenwriting to Post-Production · Infanti Studio
methodology.description: From screenwriting to post-production: the five stages behind an Infanti Studio stop motion film, with needle-felted puppets and crocheted wool sets.
methodology.intro: Five stages, from the first intuition to the final frame. Each is led together, or handed to whichever of us it belongs to.

steps.title: Screenwriting
body: Every project begins with a shared process of discussion and creative exploration. Ideas, intuitions, and visual concepts are developed together before being shaped into a screenplay by Margot.
This stage allows us to structure the narrative while preserving the spontaneity and sensitivity of our initial ideas.
steps.alt: Handwritten preparation notes pinned to a wall above a desk, with an open notebook and a shooting plan

steps.title: Visual Development
body: Louise develops the film's visual world through concept sketches and storyboards. She explores shapes, textures, and atmospheres while translating the story into a sequence of images.
This stage is essential for establishing the project's visual language and rhythm, providing the foundation that guides the animation process.
steps.alt: Open sketchbook showing blue ballpoint character concept drawings

steps.title: Fabrication
body: Based on the drawings, Margot gives the characters and sets a tangible, physical form. The puppets are built around wire armatures and covered with needle-felted wool.
The sets are also crafted from wool, using needle felting and crochet techniques, with a focus on natural, organic materials. This stage grounds the film in a tactile, handcrafted aesthetic.
steps.alt: A needle-felted puppet face resting on a workbench beside a makeup palette

steps.title: Animation
body: We animate together, frame by frame, through a meticulous and patient process.
Every movement is created by hand, gradually bringing the characters and their world to life.
steps.alt: Hands adjusting a needle-felted puppet on a red set, behind a camera mounted on a tripod

steps.title: Post-Production
body: Louise oversees the post-production stage, adding subtle 2D details such as eyelids and pupils. These elements are carefully designed to blend seamlessly with the physical materials, matching the texture of the wool.
We strive to make this stage as invisible as possible, preserving the coherence, tactility, and material presence of the image.
steps.alt: A hand drawing with a stylus on a graphics tablet, retouching a puppet's face frame by frame
